title: Same inputs, same factory: why determinism matters in 2026
description:
A factory that improves itself run against run is running an experiment, and an experiment only says something when everything except the treatment is held fixed. This whitepaper reviews the evidence for reproducibility as a requirement in 2026 (the reproducibility deficit in computational research, attacks on the software supply chain, the EU Cyber Resilience Act, and the nondeterminism of large language model inference), shows that functional package management delivers reproducible environments at scale, and reads the ouroboric-dev repositories for what their software factory already pins and what it leaves to chance.

It reports two rebuild experiments with Nix (GNU hello, and an OCI image of the factory's check tools, both bit-identical on rebuild) and proposes six ways the picasso Nix labs can close the gap, each mapped to the Yggdrasil v0 specification, with an evaluation plan and the limits of what a package manager can and cannot fix.
